name: Umbrae
source: the LINE & CYCLE look-dev the product itself ships — umbrae/docs/design/umbrae-lookdev.html, its :root tokens and its Identity + Doctrine sections, read 2026-08-31. Not an interpretation of the brand: the same values the running interface is drawn from.
positioning: The first DLMM engineered natively for EVM, live on Base — a hybrid venue where anyone can swap and provide liquidity without permission, and where concentrated, actively managed liquidity is available to those who want it.
audience: Liquidity providers and traders on Base who want their capital concentrated where it actually earns, and who read the contract before they read the marketing.
pillars: capital efficiency — liquidity concentrated where it works, not spread across prices a token will never reach
zero-fee position management — entry, exit and repositioning cost nothing but gas, so an LP can always defend a position
guarantees in code, not in promises — permissionless withdrawal and immutable fee parameters are contract-level, not policy
restraint — the instrument stays quiet until something is genuinely happening
boilerplate: Umbrae is a hybrid decentralized exchange on Base, built by Ignis AI Labs. It runs two pool types — a Dynamic AMM for hands-off liquidity and a Dynamic Liquidity Market Maker for concentrated positions — as the first DLMM engineered natively for EVM rather than ported from another chain.
voice: Instrument-quiet. Plain, exact and unhurried; the numbers carry the weight and the sentence gets out of their way. Risk is named in the same breath as return, because the FAQ already does — the brand never says two different things in two places.
tone: Level on launches: the fact, the number, the date. Factual and immediate on incidents, with what is known kept apart from what is not yet known. Never celebratory about price.
bannedPatterns: guaranteed returns, risk-free, or any phrasing implying principal is protected
projected, expected or annualised yield figures
to the moon, LFG, wagmi, gm, and the rest of that register
urgency manufactured out of nothing — last chance, don't miss out, act now
naming a competitor in order to rank against them
colour or glow used as decoration rather than as data

approved: the first DLMM engineered natively for EVM — an original architecture, not a Solana port and not a Liquidity Book fork
LPs keep 95% of every fee their pool generates at launch, with the protocol share falling to a permanent 3% floor at $10B cumulative volume
LP entry, exit and repositioning are zero-fee — network gas only
LP withdrawal is permissionless; no admin function exists that can lock user funds
fee parameters are immutable once a pool is deployed
the DLMM is audited by HashLock, with a follow-up audit completed for expanded functionality
$U1 is a fixed-supply, non-inflationary ERC-20 on Base
swapping and adding liquidity to existing pools is fully permissionless; pool creation is permissioned by design, to stop griefing
the pool uses a volatility-based dynamic fee rather than a private mempool
forbidden: any projected or expected APY or yield figure, and any past figure framed as an indication of future return
any claim that principal is protected or that impermanent loss is eliminated — IL is a real risk of liquidity provision and is always named as one
any claim that the DAMM carries the same external audit standing as the DLMM — the DAMM is audited internally
describing planned audits, planned bug bounties or in-development features as though they are already live
any price prediction, and any framing of $U1 as an investment
any statement about another Ignis AI Labs product's economics — the 40% split and the tier structure apply to Umbrae only
any figure not read from the platform's own live data at the moment of writing

disclosures: Providing liquidity carries risk, including impermanent loss.
Verify the $U1 contract address only at umbrae.io or ignislabs.ai — never from a link in a message.
Umbrae and Ignis AI Labs never DM first offering support, and never ask for seed phrases, private keys, or wallet verification.

logoRules.clearSpace: clear space on every side equal to the height of one eye-slit of the mask
misuse: never stretch, rotate, skew or redraw the mask — always reproduce it from the master vector
never add drop-shadows or gradients beyond the directional glow used on cards
never tint outside the approved set: white, rise green, fall red
never place the mark on a busy or mid-tone background — it sits on the void or a near-black surface
never substitute a system font for the wordmark; it is a vector, not type

imagery.direction: Instrument photography and interface capture: near-black, monochrome, hairlines held under 12% white. The mask on the void. Charts and figures ARE the image — the product is the picture.
avoid: stock photography of people, handshakes and offices
rocket ships, moons, bulls, bears and every other price metaphor
mid-tone or busy backgrounds behind the mark
gradients and glows that carry no meaning
